account.definition: a record that shows increases and decreases in a particular item such as cash, sales, or rent.

account balance.definition: Account balance is the amount left in an account after adding and subtracting all money in and out at a certain time.

accounting period.definition: the length of time for which financial records are prepared, such as a month or a year

activity-based budgeting.definition: a budgeting method that plans spending based on the activities that create value for the business

adjusted cash book.definition: a cash book that has been updated to include missing items and corrections before preparing a bank reconciliation statement.

adjusted trial balance.definition: a trial balance prepared after correcting errors and updating account balances.

adjusting item.definition: an item that must be entered or corrected in the cash book so the balance becomes up to date

adjusting items.definition: entries that must be added or corrected to make the records accurate

adjustment.definition: a change made to improve or correct something

allocate.definition: to give or assign money or resources to a particular use

altered cheque.definition: An altered cheque is a cheque that has been changed after it was written, often to cheat or steal money.

analysis column.definition: a special column used to group similar expenses or items in a book of account.

analytical expense column.definition: a special column in the petty cash book used for a particular type of expense

asset.definition: something valuable owned by a business, such as cash or equipment

assets.definition: things a business owns that have value, such as cash, buildings, or equipment.

balance.definition: the amount remaining in an account after comparing money in and money out

balance brought down.definition: the opening balance written at the start of the next period

balance c/d.definition: the balance carried down to the next stage of an account before it is brought forward.

balance carried down.definition: the closing balance written at the end of an account for one period

bank.definition: a financial institution where money is kept, deposited, or withdrawn for business use.

bank account.definition: a record at a bank where money is kept, received, or paid out

bank charges.definition: fees taken by the bank for services it provides.

bank column.definition: the part of a cash book where money paid into or out of the bank is recorded

bank overdraft.definition: a situation where more money is withdrawn from a bank account than is available

bank reconciliation statement.definition: a statement prepared to explain and match the difference between the cash book bank balance and the bank statement balance.

bank statement.definition: a report from the bank showing money paid in, money paid out, and the balance in an account.

banking.definition: the use of a bank to keep, send, receive, or manage money

banking transaction.definition: a money activity that happens through a bank account, such as depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money

bearer cheque.definition: a cheque that can be paid to whoever presents it to the bank

book of original entry.definition: the first place where a business transaction is recorded

book-keeping.definition: the process of recording a business’s money activities, such as what it receives and what it pays

book-keeping error.definition: a mistake made when recording, posting, or balancing accounts.

budget.definition: a financial plan that shows expected income and spending for a certain period

budgetary control.definition: checking actual spending and income against the budget and taking action when needed

budgeting.definition: the process of planning how money will be received and spent

bursar.definition: A bursar is a person in a school, college, or university who manages money and funds.

business expansion.definition: the growth of a business by increasing its size or activities

capital.definition: money or other resources invested by the owner to start or run a business

carriage inwards.definition: the cost of bringing purchased goods into the business

cash.definition: money in the form of notes and coins that can be used directly to pay for something

cash account.definition: a record that shows money received in cash and money paid out in cash

cash book.definition: a book used to record all cash received and cash paid by a business

cash budget.definition: a plan that shows expected cash coming in and cash going out during a certain period

cash column.definition: the part of a cash book where cash received or paid is recorded

cash discount.definition: a price reduction given when payment is made within a stated time.

cash float.definition: the fixed amount of cash given at the start for petty cash use.

cash flow.definition: the movement of money into and out of a business

cash inflow.definition: money that comes into a person’s or business’s hands

cash outflow.definition: money that goes out to pay for expenses or other costs

cash payment.definition: money paid out by a business and recorded in the cash book

cash receipt.definition: money received by a business and recorded in the cash book

cash shortage.definition: a situation where there is not enough cash to pay for needs or expenses

cash transaction.definition: a payment or receipt in which physical money is used

cashier.definition: a person responsible for receiving, paying, and handling cash in a business.

casting error.definition: a mistake in adding up figures in an account or book

cheque.definition: a written instruction telling a bank to pay a stated amount of money

cheque clearing.definition: Cheque clearing is the process of moving money from one bank account to another to complete a cheque payment.

cheques register.definition: A cheques register is a record used to list cheques written and their details, such as cheque numbers and payments.

clearing.definition: the process the bank uses to confirm and complete a cheque payment

closing balance.definition: the amount of money left at the end of a period

commission.definition: an error where the correct amount is entered but in the wrong account

commission income.definition: money earned for selling or arranging sales for others.

compensating error.definition: an error that is cancelled out by another error, making the totals still appear correct

compensating errors.definition: two or more errors that cancel each other so the trial balance still agrees.

complete reversal.definition: an error where the debit and credit sides are recorded the opposite way round

complete reversal of entries.definition: an error in which debit and credit entries are made on the wrong sides of the accounts.
variations: error of complete reversal of entries

comprehensive.definition: including all or almost all important parts

contra entry.definition: an entry recorded on both sides of a cash book because it affects cash and bank at the same time

corrective action.definition: a step taken to fix a problem or improve a situation

cost.definition: the amount of money needed to buy, do, or produce something

cost driver.definition: A cost driver is something that causes the cost of a product or service to increase or decrease.

credit.definition: an entry on the right side of an account; for asset accounts, it usually shows a decrease

credit balance.definition: an amount recorded on the credit side; in this topic, it can show money owed to the bank or an overdraft

credit terms.definition: the conditions that explain when and how a customer must pay for goods bought on credit.

credit transfer.definition: money received directly into a bank account from another account

creditor.definition: a person or business that is owed money by the business

crossed cheque.definition: a cheque marked with lines to show it must be paid into a bank account, not as cash

current account.definition: a bank account used by businesses for frequent deposits and withdrawals, often by cheque

current asset.definition: an asset that is expected to be used, sold, or turned into cash within a short time, usually one year

current liability.definition: a debt or obligation that a business is expected to pay within a short time, usually one year

daybook.definition: a book of original entry where transactions are first recorded before posting to ledgers.

debit.definition: an entry on the left side of an account; for asset accounts, it usually shows an increase

debit balance.definition: an amount recorded on the debit side; in a bank account, it often shows money available in the account

debt.definition: money that is owed to another person or organisation

debtor.definition: a person or business that owes money to the business

deficit.definition: A deficit happens when spending is more than income during a period of time.

deposit.definition: money paid into a bank account

deposit in transit.definition: money already recorded in the cash book as deposited but not yet shown in the bank statement

deposits in transit.definition: money already paid into the bank but not yet shown on the bank statement

depreciation.definition: the decrease in value of an asset over time because of use or age

direct credit.definition: money paid directly into a bank account

direct debit.definition: a payment that the bank takes automatically from an account

direct deposit.definition: money paid straight into a bank account without using a cheque

direct transfer.definition: money moved directly from one bank account to another

disbursement.definition: Disbursement is the payment of money for expenses or duties that must be paid.

discount.definition: a reduction in the normal price of goods or services.

discount allowed.definition: a discount given by the business to customers who pay within the agreed time

discount received.definition: a discount gained by the business when it pays suppliers within the agreed time

discounts allowed.definition: reductions in price given by a business to its customers.

discounts received.definition: reductions in price received by a business from suppliers or sellers.

discrepancy.definition: a difference between two amounts or records that should match

dishonoured.definition: not accepted or paid by the bank

dishonoured cheque.definition: a cheque that the bank refuses to pay.

dividend.definition: money paid to the owner or shareholder as a share of profit

double entry.definition: a recording system in which every business transaction affects at least two accounts

doubtful debts.definition: money owed to a business that may not be paid back

drawee.definition: the bank that is ordered to pay the money written on a cheque

drawer.definition: the person who writes or issues a cheque

drawings.definition: money or goods taken from the business by the owner for personal use.

endorsed.definition: signed on the back of a cheque to approve it for payment or transfer

error.definition: a mistake made when recording or processing money transactions

error of commission.definition: an error made when the correct amount is entered in the wrong person's account or similar wrong account.

error of omission.definition: an error that happens when a transaction is completely left out of the accounts.

error of original entry.definition: an error where the wrong amount is first entered and then posted correctly to the accounts.

error of principle.definition: an error that happens when an amount is entered in the wrong type or class of account.

estimate.definition: a careful guess of an amount or cost

expenditure.definition: money spent by a person or business

expense.definition: money spent by a person or business

expense account.definition: an account used to record money spent on a particular business cost

expenses.definition: costs a business pays in order to operate.

favourable balance.definition: a positive balance showing that there is money available in the bank account

financial obligation.definition: a payment or duty to pay money that a person or business must meet

financial position.definition: the state of a business’s money and property at a certain time

financial stability.definition: a condition where money is managed well and there are no serious money problems

financial statement.definition: a formal report that shows the financial activities and position of a business

financial statements.definition: formal reports that show the financial performance and position of a business

financial target.definition: a money goal that a person or business plans to achieve

flexible.definition: able to change or adjust when conditions change

folio.definition: a reference column used to show where related entries can be found

fraud.definition: dishonest action meant to cheat or steal money or property.

general journal.definition: a book where transactions and corrections are first recorded before posting to accounts.

general ledger.definition: the main ledger that contains all the accounts of a business

goal-oriented.definition: focused on achieving a specific aim or result

goods.definition: things that are made or sold for people to buy and use

imprest.definition: an amount of money given in advance for making payments, to be accounted for later

imprest system.definition: a petty cash system where a fixed amount is given and later restored by the amount spent

incremental budgeting.definition: a budgeting method that starts with the previous budget and makes small changes to it

inflow.definition: money coming into a business or account

insufficient funds.definition: not having enough money in the bank account to make a payment

insurance premium.definition: the money paid regularly for insurance cover

interest.definition: money earned from saving or investing money, or money paid for borrowing

interest income.definition: money earned from lending money or keeping money in an account.

inventory.definition: goods a business has on hand for sale or use.

invoice.definition: a document showing goods sold or bought and the amount to be paid.

journal.definition: a book of original entry where transactions are first recorded

journal entry.definition: the first accounting record made to show a transaction.

ledger.definition: a book or record where business accounts are kept

liabilities.definition: amounts a business owes to other people or organizations.

liability.definition: an amount a business owes to other people or organizations.

liquidity.definition: the ability to have enough cash or easily available money to pay what is owed

loan.definition: money borrowed that must be paid back later

monitor.definition: to watch and check something regularly to see how it is going

motor expenses.definition: costs related to using and running a vehicle for business.

negative balance.definition: a balance below zero, showing that more money has gone out than is available

net cash flow.definition: the difference between total cash received and total cash spent

non-current asset.definition: a long-term asset that a business uses for many years, such as machinery or furniture

notification.definition: an official message giving information about something, such as a dishonoured cheque

offset.definition: to cancel the effect of another entry or amount

omission.definition: an error where a transaction is left out completely from the books

open cheque.definition: a cheque that can be paid in cash or deposited into an account

opening balance.definition: the amount of money available at the beginning of a period

original entry.definition: the first recording of a transaction in the books

outflow.definition: money going out of a business or account

outstanding cheque.definition: a cheque that has been issued but has not yet been paid by the bank

overcast.definition: a total that is added up too high

overcasting.definition: an addition error where the total is more than the correct amount.

overdraft.definition: a negative bank balance caused by taking out more money than is available in the account

overdrawn balance.definition: a bank balance below zero, showing that money is owed to the bank

overspending.definition: spending more money than planned or more than is available

overstatement.definition: an amount shown as more than it really is.

payable.definition: money the business owes to a supplier or other party.

payee.definition: the person who is to receive the money on a cheque

payment.definition: money that is given to buy something or to settle a debt

petty cash.definition: a small amount of cash kept for minor day-to-day expenses

petty cash book.definition: a cash book used to record small daily payments

petty cash float.definition: the fixed amount of petty cash given to start making small payments

petty cash fund.definition: the amount of money set aside for making small payments

petty cash period.definition: the time between receiving petty cash and receiving the next replenishment

petty cashier.definition: the person responsible for making and recording small cash payments

petty payment.definition: a small cash payment for minor business expenses

post-dated cheque.definition: a cheque written with a future date, so it cannot be cashed until that date.

posting.definition: the process of transferring entries from books of original entry to ledger accounts.

presented.definition: taken to the bank for payment

principle.definition: an error where a transaction is recorded in the wrong type or class of account

prioritise.definition: to decide what is most important and deal with it first

profit.definition: the money left after total expenses are subtracted from total income.

purchase invoice.definition: a bill received for goods or services bought.

purchases.definition: goods or items bought by a business

purchases journal.definition: a book used to record goods bought on credit.

purchases ledger.definition: the ledger that contains accounts of suppliers from whom the business buys on credit

purchases return journal.definition: a book used to record goods returned to suppliers.

quantity discount.definition: a discount given when a customer buys a large amount of goods.

receipt.definition: money that is received by a person or business

receivable.definition: money owed to the business by a customer.

reconciliation.definition: the process of comparing two records to make sure they agree and to explain any differences

reconciling.definition: comparing two records and explaining any differences so they agree.

reconciling item.definition: an item that explains why the cash book balance and bank statement balance are different, usually because of timing

reconciling items.definition: items that explain the difference between the cash book and the bank statement

record-keeping.definition: the act of keeping clear and accurate written information about activities or transactions

reimbursement.definition: money paid back to replace what was spent

rent.definition: money paid for the use of a building, room, or land.

replenishment.definition: the act of replacing money that has been spent so the original amount is restored

resource.definition: something useful, such as money, time, or materials, that can be used to do work

resource allocation.definition: the process of deciding how money, time, or materials will be used

revenue.definition: money earned by a business from its activities, especially from sales

sales.definition: goods or services sold by a business for money

sales journal.definition: a book used to record goods sold on credit.

sales ledger.definition: the ledger that contains accounts of customers who buy on credit

sales return journal.definition: a book used to record goods returned by customers.

sales returns.definition: goods that customers return after buying them

services.definition: work done for someone instead of selling a physical product

single-column cash book.definition: a cash book with one money column on each side for recording cash only

source document.definition: an original document used as evidence to record a transaction.

stale cheque.definition: a cheque presented too late, usually after many months, so the bank may refuse to pay it

standing order.definition: an instruction to a bank to pay a fixed amount regularly to someone.

statement of financial position.definition: a financial statement that shows what a business owns, owes, and the owner’s interest at a certain date

stationery.definition: office materials such as paper, pens, notebooks, and envelopes

subsidiary ledger.definition: a ledger that contains detailed individual accounts, such as customers or suppliers.

supplier.definition: a person or business that provides goods or services to another business

surplus.definition: A surplus happens when income is more than spending during a period of time.

suspense account.definition: a temporary account used when a difference or unclear entry cannot yet be explained

taxes.definition: Taxes are required payments made by people and businesses to the government.

three-column cash book.definition: a cash book with three money columns, usually for cash, bank, and discount

time-bound.definition: limited to a set period of time

trade discount.definition: a reduction in listed price usually given by a seller, often not recorded in the accounts.

trade payable.definition: money the business owes to suppliers for goods or services bought on credit.

trade payables.definition: amounts the business owes to suppliers for goods or services bought on credit

trade receivable.definition: money owed to the business by customers who bought goods or services on credit.

trade receivables.definition: amounts owed to the business by customers who bought on credit

transaction.definition: an action in which money is paid, received, or transferred

transfer.definition: the movement of money from one account or person to another

transposition.definition: a mistake caused by reversing the order of digits, such as writing 65 instead of 56

transposition error.definition: an error made when digits are written in the wrong order, such as writing 64 instead of 46.

travelling expenses.definition: costs paid for travel, such as bus fare, taxi fare, or other transport for work

trial balance.definition: a list of account balances prepared to check whether the debit and credit totals are equal

two-column cash book.definition: a cash book with two money columns, usually for cash and discount

unadjusted cash book balance.definition: the cash book balance before missing items and errors are corrected

uncleared deposit.definition: money deposited into the bank that has not yet been fully processed by the bank

uncredited cheque.definition: a cheque paid into the bank that has not yet been added to the account by the bank.

undercast.definition: a total that is added up too low

undercasting.definition: an addition error where the total is less than the correct amount.

unforeseen expenses.definition: costs that happen unexpectedly and were not planned for

unilateral error.definition: an error that affects only one side or one part of the double entry.

unpresented cheque.definition: a cheque issued by the business that has not yet been presented to the bank for payment.

value-based budgeting.definition: a way of planning money by giving more funds to the most important goals and priorities

vendor.definition: A vendor is a person or business that sells goods or services.

voucher.definition: a document used as proof that a payment has been made

vouching.definition: checking accounting entries against source documents to confirm they are correct

wages.definition: money paid to workers for their work.

withdraw.definition: to take money out of a bank account.

withdrawal.definition: money taken out of a bank account

zero-based budgeting.definition: a budgeting method where every expense must be explained and approved starting from zero
